ava_lesson_intro.ava_speaks: CS1B · IAM: The Digital Keycard System. Ren teaching mode on.

blocks.ava_speaks: EC2-ல server rent பண்ணிட்டோம், S3-ல files store பண்ணிட்டோம். But இதுக்கெல்லாம் யாருக்கு access இருக்கு? யாராவது வந்து delete பண்ணிட்டா என்ன பண்றது? That brings us to Pillar 3: AWS IAM.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: IAM stands for 'Identity and Access Management'. Jargon-அ விடுங்க. IAM is simply the digital keycard system of your AWS account. It acts as the ultimate security guard for your cloud.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: Real world-ல நிறைய startups பண்ற தப்பு என்னனா, they share the 'Root Account' login with all developers to keep things simple. Root account is the master key to everything.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: ஒரு junior developer-ஓட password leak ஆனா கூட, attacker will take full control. அவங்க ஆயிரக்கணக்கான EC2 servers launch பண்ணி crypto mine பண்ணுவாங்க. ₹12 lakh bill in 45 minutes! This actually happens to real startups.

board_actions.text: Root Account = Master Key with unlimited power.
One leaked password = complete account takeover.

whiteboard_data.heading: The Danger of Root Access
points: Root Account = Master Key with unlimited power.
One leaked password = complete account takeover.

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: To stop this, we use IAM. When someone logs in, IAM checks two things: 1. Authentication (Who are you? - using password/MFA) and 2. Authorization (What are you allowed to touch?).
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: We control Authorization using 'Policies' (written rules). Oru data analyst-க்கு S3-ல இருந்து files read பண்ண மட்டும் தான் access வேணும்னா, அத மட்டும் தான் குடுக்கணும். EC2 access குடுக்க கூடாது. We call this the 'Principle of Least Privilege'.

board_actions.text: Give only the exact permissions needed.
Uses IAM Policies to enforce rules.

whiteboard_data.heading: Principle of Least Privilege
points: Give only the exact permissions needed.
Uses IAM Policies to enforce rules.

blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: Never give full admin access unless absolutely needed. IAM is your digital bouncer. Concepts clear-ஆ? You are now ready to configure this service in the real terminal.
blocks.speaker: Ren

workspace_tasks.question: A new EdTech startup in Bangalore wants to share the AWS Root Account credentials with their 10 new engineering interns so they can learn fast. Why will Ren completely block this decision?
options: Because AWS limits the Root Account to a maximum of 5 concurrent logins.
Because the Root Account is the Master Key. If one intern accidentally leaks the password, attackers get full control of the account and can rack up massive bills.
Because logging in with the Root Account is slower than using standard IAM user accounts.
Because IAM automatically deletes Root Accounts when they are shared with too many people.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: Root account = Master key. Never share it. intern password leak do, full account takeover. ₹12 lakh bill in 45 minutes. Always create individual IAM users.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_wrong: Root account = Master key. Never share it. intern password leak do, full account takeover. ₹12 lakh bill in 45 minutes. Always create individual IAM users.
workspace_tasks.explanation: Root account = Master key. Never share it. intern password leak do, full account takeover. ₹12 lakh bill in 45 minutes. Always create individual IAM users.

workspace_tasks.question: GreenMeter's sustainability intern only needs to download weekly CSV exports from one reports S3 bucket — nothing else. Manager wants them 'productive by lunch.' Least-Privilege move?
options: Hand them AdministratorAccess so they never get blocked.
Grant S3 + EC2 + RDS 'just in case the internship expands'.
Share the Root password and tell them verbally to only open that bucket.
Attach an IAM policy that allows read-only on that specific reports bucket and nothing else.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: Least Privilege = exactly the reports read they need. Verbal Root trust is not a control plane.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_wrong: Don't over-grant for convenience. One bucket, read-only, coded in IAM — that's Least Privilege for GreenMeter.
workspace_tasks.explanation: Least Privilege = exactly the reports read they need. Verbal Root trust is not a control plane.
